minifloat.d: A floating-point format with few bits (8, 6 or 4): sign, biased exponent and a short mantissa. The ruler is logarithmic, with the same number of values in each power of 2. Examples: FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, FP4 E2M1.

fp8-e4m3.d: An 8-bit float: 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits (bias 7), 3 mantissa bits. The “fn” variant has no ±∞ and reserves only S.1111.111 for NaN, which is why it reaches 448. Relative error ≤ 6.25%. It is the FP8 used for weights, activations and the KV cache in inference.

fp8-e5m2.d: An 8-bit float with 5 exponent bits (bias 15) and 2 mantissa bits, IEEE-style (it has ±∞ and NaN). Maximum 57,344 and relative error ≤ 12.5%: more range, less precision. Traditionally used for gradients; in the recipes it only shows up as the fp8_e5m2 KV option.

fp4-e2m1.d: A 4-bit float: 1 sign bit, 2 exponent bits (bias 1), 1 mantissa bit. Magnitudes {0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6}, 15 distinct values, no ∞ and no NaN. On its own it errs by up to 25%; it only works with a per-block scale (NVFP4, MXFP4).

amax.d: The largest absolute value of a group (tensor, row, block). The typical scale is amax / format maximum (448 in E4M3, 6 in E2M1), which takes the largest element to the top of the ruler.

fp8-block-scales.d: FP8 quantization in which each 2D tile of the weight (e.g., 128×128) has its own scale (weight_scale_inv) and the activation gets a dynamic scale per block of 128 along K. DeepSeek-V3 style; in ModelOpt it is FP8_BLOCK_SCALES. The block must be read from the checkpoint (group_size), never guessed.

weight-scale-inv.d: Name (inherited from DeepSeek-V3) of the tensor of per-block scales for FP8 weights. Despite the “inv”, it is the factor that multiplies in dequantization. vLLM's Fp8MoEMethod expects this name.

escala-e8m0.d: A 1-byte scale that stores only an exponent: the byte e is worth \(2^{e-127}\) and 0xFF is NaN. Multiplying by it is exact and cheap, but the framing moves in 2× jumps. It must be reinterpreted (view or byte << 23), never converted numerically.

ue4m3.d: An E4M3 used as a positive scale (the sign is unused), as in NVFP4's per-16 block scale. It has 3 mantissa bits, so it can be ~1.125·2^k, 1.25·2^k and so on, not just powers of 2.

lut-dequant.d: A lookup table that translates a low-bit code into its value. For FP4 E2M1, 8 magnitudes (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6) + the sign bit are enough; the result is then multiplied by the scale.

nibble.d: Half a byte (4 bits). FP4 formats store two codes per uint8. In Qwen's NVFP4 PLE, the low nibble is the even element. That is why FP4 tensors show up in checkpoints as U8 with half the columns.

microscaling-mx.d: An Open Compute Project standard: blocks of 32 elements share an E8M0 scale. The elements can be FP8 (MXFP8), FP6 (MXFP6), FP4 (MXFP4) or INT8 (MXINT8). The shared exponent is \(\lfloor\log_2 \mathrm{amax}\rfloor - e_{\max}\).

mxfp4.d: An MX format with FP4 E2M1 elements and an E8M0 scale per block of 32: 4.25 bits/value. It is the native format of DeepSeek-V4-Flash's routed experts (fp4_e8m0_k32) and of the optional indexer cache.

mxfp8.d: An MX format with FP8 elements (E4M3 or E5M2) and an E8M0 scale per block of 32: 8.25 bits/value. On the GB10, FlashInfer's mm_mxfp8 requires N, K ≥ 128 and multiples of 32; outside that, Qwen falls back to BF16 emulation.

nvfp4.d: NVIDIA's 4-bit format: E2M1 values in blocks of 16, each block with an E4M3 scale (weight_scale), plus one FP32 global scale per tensor (weight_scale_2): 4.5 bits/value. More robust to outliers than MXFP4. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's routed experts use NVFP4 W4A4.

escala-global-nvfp4.d: A per-tensor FP32 scalar, \(g = \mathrm{amax}_{\text{tensor}}/(6\cdot448)\), that places the blocks' E4M3 scales inside E4M3's range. Dequantization: code × weight_scale[block] × weight_scale_2.

input-scale.d: The FP32 global scale of the activation in an NVFP4 W4A4 checkpoint, static and calibrated offline. The activation's block scales are computed on the fly by the quantization kernel (scaled_fp4_quant).

modelopt.d: NVIDIA Model Optimizer: a toolkit that produces FP8/NVFP4 checkpoints with quant_method = modelopt. In MIXED_PRECISION mode, each module declares its algorithm in quantized_layers, with metadata also in the hf_quant_config.json sidecar.

quant-algo.d: The quantization algorithm declared per layer in a ModelOpt checkpoint: FP8, NVFP4, W4A16_NVFP4, MXFP8, FP8_BLOCK_SCALES, FP8_PB_WO, FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN… A value with no branch in vLLM's dispatch produces an unquantized layer, silently.

block-scaled-mma.d: A Blackwell tensor core instruction that receives, besides the FP4/FP6/FP8 matrices, the per-block scales, and dequantizes in the hardware itself. On SM12x: mma.sync … kind::mxf4nvf4 (FP4, ue8m0 or ue4m3 scales) and kind::mxf8f6f4; on SM100: tcgen05.mma.

compute-capability.d: The architecture version of an NVIDIA GPU, which defines its instructions and features: sm_90 (Hopper), sm_100 (datacenter Blackwell), sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) and sm_121 (the DGX Spark's GB10). The “a” suffix (12.1a) enables architecture-specific instructions.

plugin-de-quantizacao.d: An external package that registers a new method in --quantization via the vllm.general_plugins entry point, without editing vLLM. Example: DeepSeek's modelopt_gb10_hybrid, which dispatches NVFP4 between Marlin W4A16 and CUTLASS W4A4 by M.
